parts.label: Part 1
parts.article:
Hello.

Oh, hello. This is Ellie Fisher. We were at school together.

Oh, hi, Ellie. How are you? What are you doing these days?

Well, actually, I'm looking for a job, and I was wondering about applying to an airline. You know, looking after the passengers. And I heard you're doing something like that.

Yeah, I'm working as a cabin crew attendant.

Right. So, what does that involve?

Well, you might have to give them the initial safety demonstration before take-off, for example. You've probably seen that when you've made a journey by air.

Actually, I've never flown. But I'd love to. That's why I'd like a job with an airline.

Oh, right. And during the flight, you'd also be going round to see if anyone wants to buy anything.

So, I'd be dealing with money.

That's right. You'd be responsible for that. And then, of course, you'd be serving meals and snacks and things.

OK. So, can anyone apply?

Well, there are certain requirements. You must be at least 19 years old, and there's also a minimum height. That's 168 centimeters. That's to make sure you can reach the higher cupboards in the plane.

Right. I'm 169 centimeters, I think. What about qualifications?

You need to show that you have a good level of English. That's written and spoken, and also Maths.

OK. Well, I passed my exams in both those subjects, fortunately.

And it's an advantage if you can speak another language, although for cabin crew, it's not essential.

I can speak Spanish. I did that at school until I was 16.

Excellent. That'll be very useful.

And I'm pretty fit. I don't have any medical problems.

OK. Oh, and can you swim?

Yes.

Good, because that's another requirement.

Now, if you’re accepted, you’ll get a six week training course.

Right.

So that’ll cover all aspects of the job, all the basic things you need to know, and then some special things, like what action to take if a passenger suddenly has some sort of illness while you’re in the air, for example.

Right. I suppose you can’t always count on a doctor being on board.

No. And then you’ll have to do a lot of work during the training on becoming aware of the variety of cultures that your passengers may come from, and the implications of that. That’s really interesting, actually.

OK. Well, I’d definitely like to apply. What airline do you actually work for?

It’s a small airline called Eurontas. That’s E-U-R-O-N-T-A-S.

Is that N or M in the middle?

N for November. They’re good people to work for. Have a look at their website. You can download the application form from there.

Right. I don’t have much in the way of experience, though.

Well, what have you done since leaving school?

I worked in a supermarket for a bit. On the information desk, I was helping deal with queries from customers.

OK, put that down. That’s one of the most important aspects of the job, in fact.

Oh, right. And last year, I also did some voluntary work as part of a team. Should I put that down, too?

Of course. That’s something else they’ll be looking for, being able to work with others.

Right.

And a lot of airlines expect you to pay for your own uniform. But the good thing about this airline is that they provide it for you.

Great. Well, thanks so much, Greg.

analyses.content: Greg 提到需要向乘客售卖物品，Ellie 确认是否意味着要处理 money（钱），Greg 对此表示肯定。
Ellie: So, I'd be dealing with money. Greg: That's right. You'd be responsible for that.
题目已经有了 "sales"，不要重复填；注意题目是 "responsibility for..."，对应原文的 "dealing with..." 和 "responsible for that"。
Greg: ...there's also a minimum height. That's 168 centimeters. Ellie: Right. I'm 169 centimeters, I think.
Ellie 紧接着说自己是 169 厘米，这是干扰项，题目问的是职位要求（must be...），不是申请人的身高。
Greg 明确指出职位的最低身高要求是 168 厘米。
在谈到学历要求时，接待员指出需要展示出良好的英语（English）水平，同时还需要数学（maths）成绩。
这是一道简单的并列填空题，题目中给出 "English and..."，紧抓原文中 "and also..." 后面的科目词汇 maths。
Greg: You need to show that you have a good level of English... and also Maths.
Greg: And it's an advantage if you can speak another language, although for cabin crew, it's not essential.
Ellie 举例说她会 Spanish，这是具体例子，题目问的是通用条件 "one other..."，所以填 language。
Greg 提到如果你能说另一种 language（语言），那是一个优势（desirable）。
Greg: Oh, and can you swim? ... Good, because that's another requirement.
题目是 "able to..."，直接填动词原形 swim 即可，不要填 swimming。
Greg 询问 Ellie 是否会 swim（游泳），并确认这是另一个要求。
培训内容包括当乘客在飞行中突然患有某种 illness（疾病）时该采取什么行动。
Greg: ...like what action to take if a passenger suddenly has some sort of illness while you’re in the air...
"Doctor" 是干扰项（Ellie 说不能指望医生总在飞机上），不要填错。
Greg: ...becoming aware of the variety of cultures that your passengers may come from...
注意原文 "variety of..." 提示后面接复数名词，必须填 cultures。
Greg 强调培训中会涉及对乘客来自的不同 cultures（文化）的意识。
Greg: It’s a small airline called Eurontas. That’s E-U-R-O-N-T-A-S.
注意中间的 "N" 和 "M" 的发音区别，录音专门通过 "N for November" 进行了确认。
Greg 逐个字母拼写了航空公司的名字：E-U-R-O-N-T-A-S。
Ellie: And last year, I also did some voluntary work as part of a team.
题目是 "working in a..."，介词 "in" 提示后面接单数名词 team，不要填 "voluntary work"（题目括号里已有）。
Ellie 提到她作为 team（团队）的一员做过志愿工作，Greg 建议把这个写进申请里。
Greg: And a lot of airlines expect you to pay for your own uniform. But the good thing about this airline is that they provide it for you.
题目是 "You don't have to buy..."，对应原文的 "expect you to pay... But... they provide it"，负负得正。
Greg 说这家航空公司会提供 uniform（制服），所以你不需要自己买。
